settled.answer: Each race casts one Iron's Spells school 25% stronger and one 10% weaker: Human Evocation (weak Eldritch), Elf Nature (weak Fire), Dwarf Lightning (weak Ender), Orc Blood (weak Evocation), Demon Fire (weak Holy), Angel Holy (weak Blood), Hive Eldritch (weak Holy). It works through Iron's spell power attributes, so Warfront runs fine without Iron's Spells.
Captains need a level 2 base and Champions a level 4 base before an altar will summon them. Everyone else needs only a complete altar and the mana.

Base level needs two things at once: buildings on the base's mana network (wells, pylons, towers, altars) and siege waves won at a War Standard on that network. The lower of the two sets the level, so it can't be built or fought up alone. Levels 2 to 5 need 6/12/20/30 buildings and 3/8/15/25 waves. Each level allows 2 war beasts (10 at level 5). If the War Standard falls, its wave count is lost.
The Lancer-Drone is approved: a sturdy, armored four-armed ant warrior gripping a plain spear in both upper hands, rear of the haft clear of the legs, short-fingered lower hands, no throwing blade.
Sculk-dark colors; stronger underground and weaker in sunlight; Swarm raids tunnel up near their target; new Hive players start in a cave.

The Deepmaw is a lobster centaur: the lobster carapace, eight legs and tail, with an upright human-like torso and claws held out to the sides, in the Hive's sculk look, with thick claw arms and the reference's crowned face. Approved.
Beasts are rare altar units: 2 per base level, up to 10 per commander at base level 5.
Keep Warfront compatible with other mods: vanilla attributes, effects, tags and capabilities; optional integrations only.
The Hive spearman (Lancer-Drone) follows your reference: a four-armed ant-warrior with a double-bladed polearm.
The Hive gets a large burrowing beast unit based on your reference (hive-beast.png). It's a unit, not the player character.
The Demons get a large beast unit: a bone-white, skeletal flier with red barbs, insect-like wings and a scorpion stinger tail, from your reference.
Fantastical creatures come later: a few assigned to each race, most of them neutral.

Most player races get their own player model and some form of flight. Orcs: a jetpack or similar tech, not wings. Angels: angel wings. Elves: flight magic. Humans: undecided. Demons already fly on their wings. Not started; waiting on your references.
The Hive becomes a Warden and sculk-like underground race that builds its keeps in caves. Redesign comes after the mana system.
Imps are one demon species. They only fill the Impaler and Firecaster roles.
Builders, farmers and guards look plain and humanoid in every race.
Mana is base power: wells store it, pylons extend range, towers and the altar draw from it. No personal mana bar.
Manabloom grows shards (everyday fuel); mana ore gives crystals (dense fuel and building material).
Units are summoned at a multiblock altar with a menu.
Oryx-style head, bare hands and feet, wings that fold at the elbow, flight without an elytra.
